notes:
Slice L7 covers D-076 (log.md:2624-2643), D-092 (3107-3125) and D-161 (6263-6282). All three are ratified, so there is no superseded chain to follow. The chains I did follow end at ratified entries: D-165 is superseded by D-194, which is ratified; D-220 and D-267 are ratified, and so are D-214, D-174 and D-310. Every D-nnn and § link in the three Positions resolves. D-076's Position cites nothing.

All ten findings are drift, and each names the later ratified entry that records the move. D-267's renames left the D-076 Position stale for `init_*` and `workspace`. D-165 and D-194 deleted `local_types`. D-214 cut the six severity values down to two, `error` and `warning`, and turned `service` into a raised stage. D-174 retired the `interactive` marker and D-310 withdrew `needs_calling_task`. Because the log is never rewritten, every fix is an annotation. For `input_types` and `output_types` the entry's own 2026-09-25 annotation already records the rename. I kept them as rows only because the lead rule requires a row for each lead.

The leads all end in rows. `_types` and `get_` are suffix and prefix patterns, both ok. `input_types`, `output_types`, `local_types`, `init_`, `service`, `interactive` and `needs_calling_task` are findings.

D-161 rejects "renaming any of them now", and the code does not do that: `loop`, `trace`, `latest`, `binding` and `phase_bodies` all still exist.

There are three ptr claims, none false. Two are in D-092: the kind set is a normative table in Appendix C, and the table's columns are kind name, payload, owning section and severity. Since D-214 the table also has raised and policy columns. The third is D-161's sentence that the audit list grows.
